stem: Bush's broken tax pledge is often cited as a reason for his defeat in 1992. Which of the following best explains why the broken pledge hurt him so badly?

options.text: Democratic voters punished him for cutting taxes too deeply
options.misconception: Democratic voters opposed Bush for other reasons; the pledge mattered to conservatives, not to Democrats.

options.text: The pledge had been a secret promise, so voters never learned he broke it
options.misconception: The pledge was a famous public promise, repeated through the 1988 campaign — voters knew it well.

options.text: Breaking the pledge ended the Cold War and cost him his foreign-policy record
options.misconception: The Cold War ended on its own course; the broken pledge had nothing to do with it.

options.text: It convinced many conservatives that he could not be trusted on taxes and spending

rationales.A: Background: Democratic voters opposed Bush for other reasons; the pledge mattered to conservatives, not to Democrats.
rationales.B: Background: the pledge was a famous public promise, repeated through the 1988 campaign — voters knew it well.
rationales.C: Background: the Cold War ended on its own course; the broken pledge had nothing to do with it.
rationales.D: Background: for conservatives who had taken the pledge as a test of principle, the 1990 deal looked like a betrayal — and it split Bush's own coalition.
rationales.general:
1. Ask who the pledge belonged to. It was a promise to conservatives, not to Democrats.
2. Background: for conservatives who had taken the pledge as a test of principle, the 1990 deal looked like a betrayal.
3. Background: a president who breaks his signature promise loses the trust of the voters who believed it most.
4. Democrats had their own reasons to oppose Bush, and the Cold War ended on its own course.
Remember: the pledge hurt because it broke trust inside his own coalition.
